Story & Plot

Kunga faces a wildly chaotic night at a Queens momo shop just fifteen minutes before closing time. Between a homeless regular, his girlfriend bringing serious news, and immigration officers arriving for the Mexican chef, pressure mounts. When the clock strikes midnight, Kunga finds himself trapped in a time loop, reliving the same frantic fifteen minutes repeatedly.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film brings a super fun energy through its frantic time-loop premise and escalating workplace stress. Reviewers have praised its entertaining and lighthearted approach to a night gone completely wrong. The humor stems naturally from the piling disasters and Kunga's desperate attempts to handle the situation.

Performances & Direction

The cast features Tenzin Yeshi, Rinzin Ngodup, Stephanie Jeane, David Montalvo, and Francesca Gamba bringing the chaotic momo shop to life. Tenzin Yeshi also directs the project, steering the ensemble through the rapidly unfolding events. The performances keep the high-energy premise grounded and engaging.

Strengths

  • Super fun premise
  • Engaging time-loop concept
  • Charming shoestring budget execution
  • Lively ensemble cast

Weaknesses

A familiar time-loop structure runs the risk of repeating repetitive beats if not handled tightly across its runtime. The frantic pacing required to maintain the fifteen-minute loop could potentially wear thin during the second half. Additionally, the micro-budget constraints mean viewers should not expect massive technical spectacles.

Final verdict

Midnight Momo is a super fun and inventive indie comedy that makes great use of its constrained setting. Led by Tenzin Yeshi and a dedicated cast, it delivers an entertaining ride through a sci-fi time loop. Recommended for fans of creative low-budget comedies.
